title: Can Obama and Trump sway voters in the US midterm elections? #BBCNews

author: BBC News
description:
The Democrats are facing a tough midterms race in Michigan according to the opinion polls.  They suggest that the Democrat Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, is neck-and-neck with his Republican opponent Mike Rogers. 

El-Sayed, who’s from the left of the party, is an outspoken critic of Israel’s government over the war in Gaza. He’s facing a barrage of unfounded accusations, including from President Donald Trump, that he is a jihadist extremist with links to terrorism.  

Former President Barack Obama has been in Michigan campaigning for El-Sayed, in a clear sign that the Democrats are worried they could lose a key Senate seat. 

Reeta Chakrabarti presents BBC News at Ten reporting from Michigan.

author: BBC News
description:
Has Brazil turned back the tide of right-wing, pro-Trump leaders, sweeping across Latin America? Left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won re-election against Flavio Bolsonaro - the son of the jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro, whose family has close ties to Donald Trump. Analysts have described it as a stunning comeback victory, after Lula finished second to Mr Bolsonaro in the first round of voting. Mr Bolsonaro has refused to concede defeat, and is calling for the result of be annulled. 

In this episode, we look at how President Lula's campaign turned its fortunes around, and ask what grounds Mr Bolsonaro has to challenge the election outcome. Plus, we'll ask our reporter what Lula's victory means for Brazil's position in an increasingly conservative region, and the country's relationship with Washington.

title: Serbia's student-led protest movement just got elected, what now? #BBCNews

author: BBC News
description:
The student movement in Serbia was born from tragedy that began with students blockading streets and turned into almost daily protests and a national movement against corruption and government negligence.
 
In just under two years the students have succeeded in tearing up 14 years of political dominance under Aleksandar Vučić, who has seen support for his Serbian Progressive party ebb away and ultimately fail in what became a referendum on the future of Serbia.
 
Celebrations erupted in Belgrade and other cities as supporters gathered in town centres or in front of Student List headquarters. In a post on social media, the students declared "Serbia is free".

US singer Chris Brown has avoided jail after striking a man twice in the head with a glass tequila bottle in a London nightclub.
 
The R&B star was given an eight-month prison sentence, suspended for 12 months, over the attack at private members' club Tape in Mayfair, in the early hours of 19 February 2023.
 
Brown's vocal coach, rapper Omololu Akinlolu, who joined the attack, was sentenced to four months' imprisonment, suspended for 12 months. Both men, who had pleaded guilty to affray, were also ordered to pay £1,500 costs.

description:
A clean-up operation is under way in parts of the UK after Storm Boelo caused flooding and property damage, leaving thousands without power.
 
The Energy Networks Association said around 90,000 properties are still without power as of Monday.
 
Two men were killed by falling trees during the storm on Sunday - a man in his 20s in north London and another in Dumfries and Galloway in Scotland.
 
Boelo is the second storm to have hit parts of the UK in recent days, following Storm Austen which brought similar levels of disruption, while strong winds and rain are forecast to continue on Monday.

author: BBC News
description:
Prince William has told the BBC that awarding Sir Kevin Sinfield his knighthood was "probably the easiest decision that anyone's ever had to make". 
 
The Prince of Wales leads the tributes to the inspirational former Rugby League player who has raised £13 millions of pounds over seven years for motor neurone disease (MND) charities. 
 
In 2020, Sinfield went for a run after his friend and teammate Rob Burrow was diagnosed with motor neurone disease. 
 
He aimed to raise £77,777 for Rob and his family, a sum set to recognise Burrow’s number seven shirt. But just a week later, he had raised more than £2 million. It was the first of seven astonishing challenges over the next six years, which included seven ultramarathons in seven days and 101 miles in 24 hours.

author: BBC News
description:
Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar Vučić has admitted defeat to the student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections.
 
Preliminary figures from Serbia's election commission indicated a record high turnout, which commentators had suggested would favour the student movement. Celebrations erupted after Vučić conceded.
 
Vučić called the snap elections after two years of protests triggered by the collapse of a train station canopy in the city of Novi Sad, which killed 16 and was seen as emblematic of corruption and negligence.

author: BBC News
description:
Brazil's left-wing President Lula is elected for a fourth term, beating Flávio Bolsonaro in a knife-edge vote.
 
Lula, 80, had said the election was a matter of "sovereignty" and people faced a choice between someone who kissed the Brazilian flag and someone who kissed the American flag.
 
Voting was extended by two hours at some polling stations, after both campaigns pushed for it.
